paragraphs: Friend, here's the lesson that hit me hardest in this passage. The LORD says in Isaiah 17:10, "For you have forgotten the God of your salvation and failed to remember the Rock of your refuge." Cities and fortresses looked strong, but forgetting Him left them empty. I spent years in a dark drawer, and I'm telling you, no drawer is darker than forgetting the God who saves.

Now look at what people were busy doing instead. They tended their delightful plots and exotic vines like a baker watching the oven window (Isaiah 17:10-11). But the LORD says the harvest will vanish. Anything we build while forgetting Him is a batch with no staying power, and no amount of hovering fixes that.

Here's the good news, though, and I want you to hear it loud. The LORD says, "In that day men will look to their Maker and turn their eyes to the Holy One of Israel" (Isaiah 17:7). Even after the reaping, gleanings remain (Isaiah 17:6). So today, baker, look up first, and let Him be the One you remember before anything else.
